subject: Auric Labs — post-call technical qualification & SLOs
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@auriclabs.com>, Ben Cho <ben.cho@auriclabs.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-18T15:02:00Z
Subject: Auric Labs — post-call technical qualification & SLOs

Hi Elena & Ben,

Thanks again for the call today — good to see the team. Quick recap from our side (actionable items at the end):

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Inference cost is ballooning for your summarization pipeline when traffic spikes (batching-sensitive service).
- Production tail latency spikes during concurrent jobs (p99 > 1.2s on current infra).
- Model consistency: you need deterministic prompts across A/B experiments; rolling model changes have introduced regressions.

Goals you stated:
- P95 generation latency <= 200ms for 512-token median requests, P99 target <= 600ms for the same workload.
- Throughput requirement: sustained 500 qps (256-token avg) during business hours with 2x burst allowances.
- Deployment must be in a VPC (private), with audit logs and KMS-managed keys.

Technical notes from the discussion:
- Preferred model family: 13B transformer, quantized to 4-bit for cost — must support long prompt context up to 2048 tokens.
- Importance of prefix/KV caching for your UX (many requests share a ~120-token system prompt).
- You run a mix of short, latency-sensitive inference (chat + summarization) and large-batch offline reranks; need separate SLAs or routing.

Suggested topology (sketch attached as postcall-topology-diagram.png):
- Primary: Redwood Private control plane + Dedicated VCPU/GPU pool in us-west-2 (VPC peering), nodes provisioned with A10G or equivalent.
- Serving layer: model sharded across two GPU instances with a lightweight routing proxy for fast model variant fallback.
- Autoscaling: policy tuned for token-rate with warm standbys for latency SLOs; burst capacity gate to Hosted fallback in emergencies.
- Caching: Redis-backed prefix cache + local KV cache pinned in-GPU for hot sessions.

Performance estimates (empirical from similar workloads):
- 13B quantized (4-bit), sequence 512: p95 around 140–200ms when batching is tuned and KV cache hit-rate > 70%.
- Token throughput: single A10G-ish node ~650–900 tokens/sec for streaming generation depending on batch size; cluster scales linearly with sharding.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Quantization to 4-bit reduces cost but may require a short eval sweep to verify hallucination/regression on your prompts.
- Aggressive batching helps throughput but can increase tail latency for small interactive requests; trade-off handled by workload-aware split (dedicated latency service).

Next steps & owners: (high priority first)
1) Redwood & Auric joint eval — provide sandboxes with a snapshot of your production prompt set + 48-hour traffic replay. Owner: Elena (Auric) / Marcus (Redwood). Due: 2028-07-25.
2) Tech deep-dive on infra specifics (VPC peering, KMS, audit retention, allowed egress). Owner: Ben (Auric) / Priyom (Redwood). Due: 2028-07-20.
3) Prepare SLO/Cost projection table (attached auric-slo-matrix.xlsx) with three deployment scenarios: Hosted, Dedicated, Private. Owner: Sofia. Due: 2028-07-21.

Please confirm the items above and any additional constraints (e.g., specific HSM vendor, data residency beyond us-west). If this aligns, we’ll schedule the replay window and Marcus will provision a test instance with the suggested quantization profile.

Best,

Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0119

Attachments: auric-slo-matrix.xlsx, postcall-topology-diagram.png
From: Ben Cho <ben.cho@auriclabs.com>

Date: 2028-07-18T18:09:00Z
Subject: Re: Auric Labs — post-call technical qualification & SLOs

Sofia — thanks for the clear notes. Quick clarifications from our side: we can provide a 48h traffic replay but it will include PII in a few fields; need to confirm masking options. Also, our primary HSM is HashiCorp Vault with AWS KMS as backup.

On the latency SLOs — 200ms p95 sounds ambitious but acceptable if caching handles the prompt repetition; can you include a worst-case p99 estimate for cold starts? Also want to ensure streaming token-by-token output (server-sent events) is supported.

Action: Ben to reach out to Eng Ops to prepare a masked dataset and share a simple manifest by 2028-07-21.

—Ben
Ben Cho
Head of ML Engineering | Auric Labs
ben.cho@auriclabs.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-07-19T09:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Auric Labs — post-call technical qualification & SLOs

Hi Ben/Elena — small follow-up from the eng side with some numbers and a plan: 

Cold-start (no KV cache, cold model load) estimate: 1.1–1.6s p99 for full 512-token generation on a single A10G-equivalent instance. With a warm pool (persistent model loaded), cold-start p99 reduces to ~600–800ms depending on batch overlap.

Suggested experiment to validate:
- Phase 1 (sandbox): single-node warm pool, quantized 13B 4-bit; run 48h replay at 1x ramp. Measure KV cache hit-rate, p95/p99, and token cost.
- Phase 2 (scale test): 3-node sharded cluster, simulated 2x burst. Measure degradation curves and autoscale latency.

I’ll provision the sandbox (private VPC) once we have masked replay. I’ll also include a streaming SSE wrapper and an opt-in lower-latency serving path (smaller batch, reserved capacity) for interactive requests.

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
